target_stack: Spring Boot · Spring Batch · JPA/Hibernate · PostgreSQL
summary: CBACT01C reads every record from the master credit card account file (VSAM KSDS, sequential access) and distributes each account into three output files in parallel.

io_files.content: Full account details (11 fields, reformatted reissue date)
Account ID + 3 hardcoded balance/debit scenarios per account
Two record types: short (ID + status) and long (ID + bal + limit + year)

content.text: ACCTFILE is a VSAM KSDS on the mainframe. For the Java batch job, decide:

items.label: Option A — DB (recommended)
items.text: Accounts are already in PostgreSQL (populated by another migration step). Use JpaCursorItemReader<Account>.

items.label: Option B — File
items.text: Export VSAM to a fixed-length flat file (300 bytes/record). Use FlatFileItemReader with a custom FixedLengthTokenizer.

content.text: Recommendation: Option A if the Account entity exists in the target DB, otherwise Option B.
The three output files are flat binary/fixed-length. For Java:

items: Keep as flat files (FlatFileItemWriter) — drop-in replacement for downstream consumers
Write to PostgreSQL tables — cleaner for modern downstream systems

content.text: Document the choice; it affects all three ItemWriter implementations.
The array file always writes hardcoded scenario values (1005.00, 1525.00, -1025.00, -2500.00). This looks like test data generation, not production logic.
Clarify with business: is this file still needed in Java, or was it a mainframe test artefact? (See also BR-4)
The variable-length record file (2 record types per account) is unusual. Identify the downstream system(s) that read it.
If the consumer is also being migrated, the interface can be redesigned (e.g., two separate files or a DB view).
The assembler date-conversion utility is called once per account. Replace with Java DateTimeFormatter — no external call needed. See DEV-6.
Map ACCOUNT-RECORD from copybook CVACT01Y.cpy (300 bytes, app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy):
Maps OUT-ACCT-REC (11 fields). Note: OUT-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT defaults to 2525.00 when source value is zero (business rule BR-2).
Maps ARR-ARRAY-REC: account ID + 3 occurrences of (currentBalance, cycleDebit). Only 3 of the 5 array slots are populated — see business rule BR-4.

items: Short (12 bytes): VB1-ACCT-ID (11) + VB1-ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS (1)
Long (39 bytes): VB2-ACCT-ID (11) + VB2-ACCT-CURR-BAL (12) + VB2-ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT (12) + VB2-ACCT-REISSUE-YYYY (4)

content.text: OUT-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT and ARR-ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT use USAGE IS COMP-3.

items: If reading/writing raw binary files: use BigDecimal with explicit packed-decimal encoding/decoding (e.g. Apache Commons PackedDecimal or a custom codec)
If using DB or text format: BigDecimal with standard scale suffices

content.text: COBOL abends on any I/O error — set noSkip / noRetry to replicate strict fail-fast semantics. Do NOT use skip policies unless the business explicitly allows partial output.

items: DB path: JpaCursorItemReader<Account> with SELECT a FROM Account a ORDER BY a.accountId
File path: FlatFileItemReader<Account> with FixedLengthTokenizer, field widths from CVACT01Y (total 300 bytes). Map COMP-3 fields via custom FieldSetMapper.

content.text: Input: Account. Output: AccountExportResult (holds all output records). Steps per account:

items: Log all fields to SLF4J INFO (replaces 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD DISPLAY statements)
Populate flat record (replaces 1300-POPUL-ACCT-RECORD) — see DEV-6 for date conversion
Apply default debit rule (replaces IF ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT = ZERO MOVE 2525.00)
Populate array record (replaces 1400-POPUL-ARRAY-RECORD) — see BR-4
Populate short + long VBR records (replaces 1500-POPUL-VBRC-RECORD)

AccountFlatFileWriter — writes AccountFlatRecord to OUTFILE. Use FlatFileItemWriter with FormattedLineAggregator. Field widths must match OUT-ACCT-REC layout exactly if binary-compatible output is required.

AccountArrayFileWriter — writes AccountArrayRecord to ARRYFILE. Each record: account ID (11) + 3 × (balance 12 + debit 12) + filler 4 = 75 bytes. Only implement if AD-3 confirms this file is still needed.

AccountVbrFileWriter — writes two records per account to VBRCFILE. Must prepend a 4-byte RDW (Record Descriptor Word) per record if the downstream consumer expects standard mainframe variable-length format. Short: 12 + 4 = 16 bytes on disk. Long: 39 + 4 = 43 bytes on disk.

content.text: The assembler call CALL 'COBDATFT' USING CODATECN-REC (app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl:231) converts the reissue date. Input type 2 = YYYY-MM-DD, output type 2 = YYYYMMDD (no separators).
Handle blank/null input gracefully — mainframe FILLER fields may produce spaces.
Every account in the source must be processed. No WHERE clause filter, no status check.
If ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT is zero, write 2525.00 to the flat output file.

Card reissue date (ACCT-REISSUE-DATE, format YYYY-MM-DD) must be written to OUTFILE in YYYYMMDD format via DateConversionService (see DEV-6). Only the 4-digit year (YYYY) is written to the long VBR record.
The ARRYFILE logic always writes exactly 3 of the 5 possible occurrences with partially hardcoded values:
This is almost certainly test/demo data generation, not business logic. Confirm with business before implementing (see AD-3).

items: Short record (12 bytes): account ID (11 bytes) + active status (1 byte)
Long record (39 bytes): account ID (11) + current balance (12) + credit limit (12) + reissue year (4)

content.text: All 11 account fields must be logged for every processed account. Use SLF4J at INFO level. Include account ID in every log line for traceability.
Consider DEBUG level in production if account volumes are high — millions of accounts = millions of log lines.
COBOL calls 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM on any I/O failure, which calls CEE3ABD with abend code 999.

items: Throw an unchecked AccountExportException (or RuntimeException) from any writer
Configure the Step with .noSkip(Exception.class) → job stops immediately with FAILED exit status
The CEE3ABD call has no Java equivalent — JVM exit code and Spring Batch job status are sufficient for operators

content.text: COBOL explicitly checks open/close status for all four files.

items: In Spring Batch, resource open/close is handled by the framework
Verify input file exists / DB is reachable before starting the step
Wrap output resource creation in try-with-resources or Spring resource lifecycle

tasks.title: I/O status display → structured exception log

content.text: 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS decodes the 2-byte COBOL file status into a readable 4-digit code.

content.text: Replace the 11 DISPLAY statements in 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD with one structured log call in AccountExportProcessor. Use a single INFO log line per account with all fields, or DEBUG-level multi-line format.
COBOL displays VBRC-REC1 and VBRC-REC2 before writing. Implement at DEBUG level in AccountVbrFileWriter.

items: Blank/spaces input → returns 8-space string (not null, not exception)
Invalid format → exception with clear message

content.text: Use a fixed Account object. Verify:

items: BR-2: zero debit → 2525.00 in flat record
BR-2: non-zero debit → original value preserved
BR-3: date reformatted correctly in flat record
BR-3: reissue year extracted correctly in long VBR record
BR-4: array record occurrences populated with expected values
BR-5: VBR record byte lengths are 12 and 39

content.text: Write a single AccountExportResult and assert:

items: Flat record: field positions and values match OUT-ACCT-REC layout
Array record: structure and byte size match ARR-ARRAY-REC layout
VBR short record = exactly 12 bytes, correct field content
VBR long record = exactly 39 bytes, correct field content

content.text: Use @SpringBatchTest + in-memory H2 (or Testcontainers PostgreSQL). Input: 3–5 sample accounts including one with zero cycle debit and one with blank reissue date.

items: Job completes with COMPLETED status
All 3 output files contain correct record counts
Spot-check field values in each output format
Zero-debit account → 2525.00 in flat output

content.text: If sample COBOL output files are available (from a test VSAM run):

items: Run the Java job against the same input data
Byte-compare each output file against the COBOL reference output
Document any intentional differences (encoding, line endings, RDW format)

open_questions.question: Is the ARRYFILE still required downstream?
Who consumes VBRCFILE? Are they also being migrated?
open_questions.impact: May allow redesigning the variable-record interface

open_questions.question: What is the expected record volume (accounts per run)?
open_questions.impact: Determines chunk size, parallelism, and memory settings

open_questions.question: Does OUTFILE need to be byte-for-byte compatible with COBOL output (EBCDIC, packed decimal)?
open_questions.impact: Determines whether ASCII/EBCDIC conversion is needed

open_questions.question: Is COBDATFT used by other programs being migrated?
open_questions.impact: If yes, create a shared DateConversionService in a common module

open_questions.question: Are there job restart requirements (partial re-runs after failure)?
open_questions.impact: Spring Batch restart from last checkpoint vs. full re-run

open_questions.question: What replaces the CEE3ABD abend monitoring in the operations team's tooling?
open_questions.impact: May need a specific exit code or alerting hook
